chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qurashi al-Hakim narrated that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan al-Mutawwa'i al-Bukhari said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud in Baghdad narrated that Ali ibn Harb al-Malla'i said: Abu al-Salt al-Harawi said: Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) narrated from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Faith is confession by the tongue, recognition by the heart, and action by the limbs.
ai.seo_question: What are the three essential components of faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Twelve Imams, establishes the classical Shia definition of faith as a triad comprising verbal confession (iqrar), internal conviction (ma'rifah), and physical practice (amal). It underscores the integration of belief and action, a key distinction in Shia creedal theology, while linking the Prophet’s teaching directly to the Ahl al-Bayt. The emphasis on 'amal' (practice) highlights that true faith is not merely cognitive but requires tangible adherence to religious pillars.
